en: Mount Jinshan has already come to rest; the *Shiyi ji* (Collection of Relics) records that he manifested the ritual of transformation by holding a monk’s staff and a begging bowl before a Śākyamuni image.
Seated cross-legged upon a lotus, he was once again majestic and towering. What need was there for Subhūti to further extend his praise?
Please return all at once to the royal city of Śrāvastī.
Amidst the tiles and rubble of an ancient temple, a ceramic Buddha manifests light;
amidst the ashes, the ūrṇā-kośa radiates brilliantly. Neither gold, nor jade, nor sandalwood—this is a perfect, natural perfection.
Buddha! Do not regard this as an ordinary clay pot;
Master Bagu carries it on his back and shoulders to no avail. How many people of the time understand such expedient means? Why not simply cast away the cloth bag?
Very well. Return now to the Tuṣita Heaven.

Treading upon the reeds, Bodhidharma’s words of coming from the West did not meet with accord from the King of Liang. Upon ten thousand acres of autumn river, a single reed raft—merely saying "I am ashamed," he surged through the waves.
Urgent! Who would have known that upon entering the water, one would see the person’s height?

Prime Minister Pei’s mountains towered twelve spans; Huangbo held a station as weighty as the Three Ducal Ministers, aiding the Great Tang. Through the Five Dynasties, he followed the changes until the blazing Song dynasty.
Exchange. A single *hu* of mud; the *huatou* is long.
Guest Attendant Yue returns to Guoqing;

with his smoke-stained staff, he crosses the river marshes day after day. Sending off the north and welcoming the south, he does not weary of the toil. How can this compare to resting at ease this time?
Departing for the quiet place of Five Peaks to listen to the pine waves.
Seeing Off Yuan Liao:
Since meeting at Yuan Bie-feng, when has there ever been a parting? The bright moon and clear wind hang from the tip of his staff; he has traversed East Chu and West Wu.
Pervasive. Lake Tai remains as it was, spanning three prefectures.
The head monk Yao’s *Piaomiao Ji* (Collection of the Gourd):
"The Qin city was built with earth, yet the pestle had no handle; The Han founder slew the serpent, yet his sword possessed a blade. Cast it toward the sun at Fusang."
The lining. Who among the Tang people can discern where these tracks lead?
Regarding the story of Zhaozhou’s “Seven-Pound Shirt”:
the seven-pound shirt comes from Qingzhou; a single-leaf boat rests across the ancient bank. At the end of the day, the road is long, yet no one [travels it].
Crossing over—what prevents one from carrying the moon across the azure isles?
Seeing off a monk returning to Shuanglin to visit his master:
At Haimen, he personally met Master Haiyun; The river moon, round and full, seals the evening glow. The *tao* trees stand side by side as one.
Zhao. What need is there to present the perfect circle as a separate device?
Whether the guest-master arrives or not, "go drink tea. Setting out the entire tray reveals the true nature of things; since he is at home, he knows how to welcome guests well.
Guest: Why do you not begrudge me my travels? Host:

The painted cock’s crest is surrounded by autumn flowers, lowly yet towering high. Let the cock’s crown cease its vain struggle to dye itself vermilion; in the height of the Tianbao era, such things did not exist.
The elephant cannot bear to be drawn out for others to see.
On the wooden stones and mossy walls, spring brings forth ice and snow upon the branches; summer insects dare not fly near the roots. On the southern side of the stone bridge, it was once...
Behold! As several trees hold the autumn within them, a solitary crane returns.

To bid farewell to the Venerable Guang, the Great Sound rises as he extends his broad tongue. The surging waves of the Yangtze River shake the walled city; the *dhūtas* within the crags startle awake.
In stillness, even the floating Buddha of Wu swallowed his voice.

I send this precious collection for you to take with you; do not deceive me regarding this treasury. Is the West of Shu any different from the East of Wu? The courtyard cypress, though scorched by summer heat, locks its branches in silence.
Cui. In the autumn chill of the wellside paulownia, crimson leaves flutter down.
Sent off by the attendant as the rooster’s cry pierces the dawn of the fiery heavens, one has already attained the Patriarch’s pivot before the sound itself. The Yangtze River flows eastward.
At the sea, facing the current, he could not yet buy a boat to return.
Leaving the mountains, he fled the royal palace under a frosty night; his eyes were so frozen that they would not open, and he mistook the stars for the moon.
I see that the deceiver has again come forth from the Snow Mountains.

When I sent the Secretary Gao to deliver [the message], he went out his door to welcome me at the time of the sea willow flowers. Before the flowers have even faded, he urges me on my journey. How does this compare to crossing the rivers north and south?
Guests: Though we do not know one another, there is no feeling of resentment.

Seeing off Daochang, the guest prefect, for Jinling—where the spring waters of the Teao are deep and green like moss—he once used them to brew tea for those who came from afar. Many of the heroes of the Six Dynasties have sunk beneath them.
Intoxicated. What harm is there in calling them awake to give them a cup?
Inscribed on a painting of the Dragon King inviting Arhats for a meal:

Within the Dragon King’s palace, they satiated themselves with fragrant offerings; Crossing waters and piercing clouds, they toiled with their coming and going. How does this compare to soaring through the void, shaking the golden [bell]?
Xin: "Morning I roam South Peak, evening I visit Tiantai.

To send off Chief Seat Cheng with the Mahāyāna Dharma—what words can be spoken? He tried to prop up a false mountain vine to demonstrate a single pivot; Yangzi stirred the dry depths until not a drop remained.
Water: in the land of fire, it scatters and flies as snowflakes.
I bid farewell to Master Shanyuan as he pays homage at the Patriarch’s stupa.
The Way is indeed steep and rocky, impossible to pierce; the patterns of Xiangtan are likewise difficult to transmit. Seek further from a teacher of wisdom—the lapis lazuli.
O Palace Lord! A boat follows the carriage beneath the shadowless tree.

To escort Master Puxu to pay homage at the Patriarch’s stupa—embracing the jade and casting oneself upon a teacher for polishing—is it not so? Yet, if one has not yet become a vessel, what then? It does not hinder one from parting the weeds to knock at the gate of the Buddhas.
The Patriarch: Blue towers rise one after another, entangling the green vines.
In this same rhyme, I bid farewell to Master Yunyan:

At the essential paths of power, you have long been bound in fetters; though the mountains and waters are pure and splendid, how can you roam them? How much better it is to be idle and carefree in Hexi.
Scholar! The wind and moon over the Five Lakes, a single staff in autumn.
As he gathers [the flowers] to return to Mingzhou, the Master smiles;
his two eyes are alight like blossoms. Picking up the fragrance and gathering the finest blooms, he vainly boasts of their rarity; with a turn of his body, he tramples down the long sandbar.
My son, you have released the Azure Phoenix of the Central Heaven and entrusted it to Cheng Yuanchang for seventeen years across the regions of Wu and Chu;
yet not a single sound has reached the side of my verse. If you wish to know its true nature, it is never apart from you.
A union. The moon is white and the wind is clear under one sky.
Bodhidharma’s single shoe was displayed before Mount Xiong’er to reveal his secret mechanism. What sound, what trace, for people to spy upon? Without cause, he encountered the Ridge-Head.
Messenger! Who does not know this man of hidden conduct?
When he spoke with the King of Liang, their words did not meet; with a single reed across the river, he departed as if flying. Was it that for nine years there was no resolution?
Again, he took his single shoe and returned toward the West.
Dharma Master, you offered incense at Zhugan, where the school shattered the six heterodox masters; in China, the flower joined five petals in fragrance.
On this day, as I recall past events before the wind, it causes me once more to consume a censer of incense.

As he saw off the Abbot An, he cast down a piece of firewood and immediately turned back his head. Alive and well like a spinning pearl, it cannot be retained. Gazing to the end of the world from the peak of the Great Tortoise, his two eyes grow old;
how can one board the same boat with him beyond the Eastern Sea?

Half his body, Bodhidharma came from the West to this Eastern Land to transmit the mind. How could the mind be transmitted? It is but a deception to delude people. His words struck Emperor Liang, leaving him no place of refuge;
even to this day, he dares not reveal his whole body.
In praise of Master Songling of Japan:

Songling stands solitary and lofty upon the lands of海东 (Haidong). None of the four quarters fail to look up to his patriarchal style. He sat three times upon the Dharma seat, flourishing the transformation of the world;
His orthodox succession flows on continuously, rising like Mount Song.

In discerning physiognomy and celestial patterns, he could distinguish them as clearly as they appeared upon the palm of his hand; he was especially adept at the "Transformational Discourse" concerning stellar signs and avian omens. Among all matters of success and failure throughout antiquity and the present, none surpass this;
he alone was granted the rare mastery of both the roots of heaven and earth.
In teaching the Way to the monk Jishang, one must know the art of archery. Ji does not permit the loss of the first moment;
watch as he releases a single shot of a thousand-jin weight, piercing the void and dividing it into two sides.
Sent to Secretary Qin:

Your lofty stream and noble achievements are difficult for the multitude to emulate. As vast as the ocean of literature is the ocean of Dharma. With a single stroke of the brush, you dry up the waters of Yangzi;
you would be a fitting Hanlin scholar for the Zen groves.
Seeing off Chan Master Zhang as he returns to Min:
The True Teaching has no words or phrases; The ten-thousand-li long river mirrors the vast sky. A single hair swallows it all, leaving not a drop;
The rising tide capsizes Master Xie’s broken fishing boat.

Inscription on the Painting of King Wu of Zhou Fanning a Thirsty Man The Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns stand side by side through the ages; Mountains, rivers, palaces, and towers have all turned to dust. How can they compare to the enduring fragrance left by King Wu of Zhou?
For ten thousand generations, this painted scroll depicts one who refreshed the thirsty.

With the embroidered patterns of talent within his breast, he is fit for statecraft; by the stream with rod and line, he finds contentment in reclusion. How could this Great Age tolerate a man of extraordinary talent?
He dwells high aloft alone, aging through a hundred years of spring.
Praising Master Zhongfeng as he released his iron hawk before Lion Cliff:

it swallowed the white-fanged beast of the South Mountain; throughout the vast forests of the earth there is not an inch of soil left, and across the worlds of the ten directions all traces of the fox have vanished.
In the same rhyme: Sending off Attendant Hao to visit his father, Master Dugu.
The master’s forge is wondrously subtle and stern; Not only is his realization of the Way profound, but his teaching is likewise complete. As a father, he surely gave birth to such a son;
How could you flee so far away to seek instruction?
Bazu’s Dharma Words and Calligraphy on Master Zhongfeng (II) The bell from the beginning of the kalpa has never been struck;
the sword in the royal treasury has just emerged from its whetstone. To employ these two things as one requires a master hand;
otherwise, it is but a vain exertion of the body.
The Elder Huanzhu of Tianmu Mountain—though we have been separated for a time, I hope this letter reaches you. How much more so now that his passage into ultimate stillness has long been past;
how could one not feel a wind of longing for his virtue upon reading these words?
There are superior men who pay homage at the pagoda;
they are in Suzhou, and they are in Changzhou. To know that there is something beyond the personal is to rely on what is intimate.
Within the grassy thicket, eighty-four people strike out a jade qilin from the tip of their staffs.
The Ink Plum of West Lake: He-ting returned to the Three Isles; Hua-guang of South Peak departed for the Nine Provinces.
Sparse shadows slanting across distant misty waters— A single branch preserves its ancient elegance.
The Abbot Longxiang Huizang left behind a letter and presented a verse; I respond using his rhyme scheme (3):
Five thousand scrolls and more, all in total leisure and ease; Textile brocades stored within the breast, showing no speck of flaw.
Suddenly upon the river, a line cast from beyond the heavens, Calling back Shi-de and Han-shan.
The trees on Dragon Ridge have not yet turned to ash; the five-petaled flower blooms beyond the kalpas.
Boundless fragrant winds arise for those below, and a great sound shakes through the ages like spring thunder.
How could the discourse spanning vast kalpas be obscure? What is before one’s eyes is none other than King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaranādin.
Whether he has already entered parinirvāṇa or not, let the various quarters freely suppress or exalt him as they please.
Inscription on Li Ruguān’s Grapes and Dragon-beard Vine Clusters All say that the drifting sands are about to arrive; Who recognizes the cool moonlit night in the land of Zhù?
Before the wine-cup, one has shared a branch from amidst the rain.
Inscription on a Joyful Magpie (II) A joyful event is about to arrive;
its dual-toned voice first brings the news. With ink-black feathers hidden against its snowy branch, how could it have merely gathered there for the sake of flight?
Branch after branch, there are no green leaves; beneath the flowers, one vainly seeks to hide one’s person. To delight in proximity can be a foreboding omen;

how could one know that there is a hunter with his arrow? Preface to the "Rongzhai" (Studio of Tolerance): The Greatness of Emptiness contains all phenomena, yet these myriad phenomena cannot obstruct it. Therefore, it operates and circulates.
In the four seasons, he was able to preserve his vital energy (*qi*). The magnitude of his mental substance encompassed all phenomena, yet those myriad phenomena could not confuse or corrupt it;
thus, in responding to various conditions, he was able to maintain the integrity of his voice. This was the scholar-recluse Zhao Shifu.

This is called "Wisdom. It is not that the Great One has failed to comprehend this principle; rather, it is because he possesses such wisdom that why would he grasp at this? Therefore, the title *Rongzhai* (The Studio of Tolerance) is most appropriate.
I have thus revised the text with its chapter divisions and sentences as follows.

Encompassing all that exists, it never feels constrained; its wondrous function, whether horizontal or vertical, is free from peril. Dwelling loftily in a single room, with whom does he share his company?
He calls forth the birds of the nest, and together they return home.
In the year of Xinsi, at the age of seventy-three, the spirits of the mountains gave a premonition that the mountain gate would suffer a calamity within the tenth month.
On the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month, he immediately withdrew from the monastery to avoid the disaster. Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying:
This mountain monk is seventy-three this year; a crisis is imminent within these ten months. With old age and illness upon my person, it is difficult to bear heavy responsibility;
how much better to lay it down and dwell in leisure, companioning the clouds.

Soon thereafter, the monastic community did not believe him. On the fourth day of the tenth month, the head seat Mengzhe led the assembly to the retired quarters, where they earnestly entreated him to remain, refusing to allow him to depart.
Consequently, he reluctantly complied with their request and returned once more to the abbot’s quarters.
On the evening of the twenty-seventh day of that same month, the disaster indeed occurred beyond remedy, reducing the temple to ashes in a calamitous fire. Now, having passed...
It has been three years. This is recorded as a notice for the assembly:
Amidst a heap of rubble, he alone exerts himself; His head is covered in white snow, his face is smeared with dust. At seventy-six years of age, he still repays his karmic debts;
He makes the wooden figures by the riverbank laugh to their hearts' content.
Poem Presented to the Chancellor:

On Behalf of the Grand Person, A Memorial on the Extraordinary Grant of the Great Title. Vast and boundless, the mountains and rivers flow through a single path; Supporting the sun, it shines forever bright and illuminates all.
Repairing the heavens so they leak no more, it provides eternal shelter. I alone pity that the Buddhist temples cannot escape the kalpa’s end; Even the twin pagodas [of the Twin Peaks]...
Transforming emptiness—how could one turn the pivot to pursue former views? For a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, let us chant praises of primal merit.
To Xie Nangba, Administrative Assistant at Jiang Temple:
In years past you suffered the calamity of fire; today you rely on sweeping away the ashes of that kalpa’s end. The stupa bears the essentials, dividing the clouds.
Epitaph: The Brahma-realm is still beheld amidst surging waves; Planting bamboo is superior to those lacking wisdom. How could a child piling sand have achieved full merit?
Having obtained the power of your guidance to pursue the original contemplation, Your fragrance shall flow for a thousand ages, shared by a hundred blessings.

Next, following the rhyme of Qin Ziji, the literary legacy of Huaihai has been transmitted since antiquity. Who would have known that what emerged later attained the primordial state? Its accomplishment did not rely on the power of the "three surpluses" (leisure, winter, and night);

its Way was revealed through the fundamental cause of a single great condition. Leaves fall and flowers bloom, fully manifesting the wondrous essence; the warbling of orioles and the chatter of swallows are all [the Dharma].

A supplementary commentary: Having clarified that Master [Confucius] of the Eastern Lu understood the nature of things, he cast aside the "On the Equalization of Things" chapter of the *Nanhua* (Zhuangzi).
Following the original rhyme, I respond to the three gentlemen, the Licentiates Lü, Zhu, and Li:

You three have not yet been permitted to practice the "three rests. In this flourishing age seeking the worthy, even those with white hair are sought. The sea is vast and the waves deep; there the leviathans roar.

The moon; the heavens are high and the wind is sharp as cranes soar through autumn. When one’s merit is perfected, how could it require the aid of crimson-robed officials? When a verse is fine, why should it drift away with the red leaves?
After the hardship, longing for home but having no means to leave, I sit upon a heap of tiles amidst the grass and recite the "Ascending the Tower."
In the same rhyme, a reply to the Reverend Gulin for his kind letter:

Everyone says the fine mountains occupy the preeminent field; Who can, when the moment strikes, avoid falling into the ordinary? Beating through rain and beating through wind, his staff is still pungent;
Entering the mud and entering the water, he reveals his greatness to men. His great voice directly rivals the thunderclaps; His profound eloquence is difficult to match, like the ocean.
Inference: At the Phoenix Terrace, a temple has stood for a thousand ages; today, a Chan elder suddenly gives rise to many sons.
[The following is] a response in the same rhyme to the Outer Secretary of the Southern Terrace:
With frost-white brush and tongue, you utter lotus flowers; I am ashamed that this fragrance has reached my humble home. The fish-drum beats in the wind as we partake of sweet rice.
A single grain of mud from the swallows' nests, dampened by rain, stains the *kāṣāya*; the people of Gijjha-kula vie with one another to purchase the paper for the scriptures.

The Dragon Pond lies empty and marked with spots, awaiting the drafting of the imperial edicts. How could I obtain a small boat to glide over the white waves, to invite Lu Yu together to appraise the sacred tea?
In the same rhyme, a reply to Huang Xuezhou, Chief Supervisor, upon meeting by chance at Wucheng along the ancient riverbank:
I could not brew tea nor burn bamboo roots; The imperial decree once reached me from the Lesser Sea, And late in life, the golden seal was finally bestowed at the Gate of Xiaoxun.
To present counsel, one must surely ascend the high terraces; How can one remain sitting idly while the people's ailments fester?
The seat is warm; the virtues of Gong and Huang of old are seen today. One stands upon the jade steps, awaiting the clamor of tinkling girdles.
As I see off the Abbot Zang returning to his native land (in the East), we have been close at Pei Temple for several autumns.
Probing to the left and searching to the right, he emerges as a contemporary of the times. The wheel of the Dharma turns three times, turning the very source.

Purity. When both concentration and wisdom are fully articulated, wisdom need not be further cultivated. The slumbering tiger, fierce and watchful, abandons its old den; the soaring dragon, majestic and agile, stirs from the sacred pool.
May it well turn a single drop into the waters of the Chang Jiang, swelling the vast seas and lands of the East.
In the same rhyme as the preceding poem:

Before the winter solstice, snowfall is often divined by the "three whites" for agricultural purposes. Before the twelfth month, we joyfully behold these slender, fine flakes. The crane’s body, fearing the cold, is covered by drifting cotton-wool;
the horse’s hoof, stiff with frost, is burdened by its load of salt. The cloud-leaves have a sound that knocks upon the bamboo door; the celestial flowers scatter without stems.
Mao-yen: Among the forest trees, one does not recognize the auspicious signs of the fields; the tea cauldron has moved deep beside the mountain peak.
(In the same rhyme, responding to Cheng Yuanzhang on the occasion of the New Year at Ao Temple:
The year’s affairs have shifted; the shaven head is like drifting willow catkins, and the temples are streaked with silver threads. The lotus-sails, piece by piece, shield the crimson [sun].

Day. When the autumn maples shed their verdant hues in a rustling wind, The mountain moon hides behind clouds as the first light of dawn breaks through. River waves toss snow-white foam, washing away the sorrows of autumn.
At the walled citadel, one’s brow is furrowed; at the ruined city, progress is blocked. I am deeply grateful that my dear friend has sent me this poem once more.
In the same rhyme, a reply to the Chan Master Ning of Lingyan:
Long known for his many talents, yet none surpasses this new acquaintance’s singular brilliance. His iron staff flies from the vast ocean;
the golden scriptures are transmitted from the land of India. At Jianjing, he scoops the moon as the rain has just cleared; on Xiangjing, he seeks spring amidst the falling snow.
Unopened, how could one find leisure to pursue the traces of former sages? At Guqin Terrace, the *xun* and *chi* flutes play in alternation.
A verse on the restoration of the Tripitaka scrolls:
Keng Jiang of Hengyang upholds the True Teaching; he has sacrificed his stipend to welcome the scriptures back to the field of awakening. Half of the jade leaves remain pierced by iron.

The thorns are sharp; the golden seal alone secures the solid silver oar. Layer upon layer, cloud shadows merge with the reflections of the river; brilliantly, the glow of the dawn robs the sun of its light.
Having been purified and made solemn, the entire Dharma-treasury is complete; all you lords should offer praise to this worthy officer of the forest.
In the same rhyme: Seeing off Assistant Minister Songhe on his way to the Capital.
Whenever I gaze toward the gates of Wu, my eyes never rest; I rejoice that the noble steed has happily announced your entry through the pine pass. Six years have passed in vain amidst fine scenery;

A single night of pure conversation has made me forget the hardships of the year. Together we shall look upon the sun-like brow at the Phoenix Pond; The imperial decree surely shall break [the clouds].
The heavens are stingy. Come spring, around the second or third month, you shall fulfill your vow to welcome the distant mountains.

As for the reclusive scholar Mei, who has abandoned Confucianism for Buddhism—whether one chooses an official post or a Buddha, which is more appropriate? Why not shake off the dust of worldly toil and choose that upon which to rely? Du Fu’s verse is grand, yet it does not reach the ultimate.

The Way. How could the subtle artistry of Master Dong be anything but the true mechanism? One must investigate the meaning grasped upon the seat; one must not violate the resolve to clear away the weeds before the steps.
The Peak of Wisdom is lofty and the Hall of Planning is vast; in the deepening autumn, I look forward to returning to this very place.

In the same rhyme, responding to the Langzhong of the Southern Terrace, who gazed toward Shengzhou from the summit of Mount Ao: Beyond the clouds, the Frost Tower recalls the days of Ri-xiu. When the harvest is ripe, what need is there for the strength of straw dogs?
When the times are clear, how could wooden geese be allowed to drift? The sound of the tide shatters the moon over the single river; The colors of the trees adorn ten thousand peaks.
Autumn in the Valleys. The vital energy of the Great Mass is solemn; talent and spirit are both present. Do not forget your green shoes as you traverse the celestial journey.
"Recalling an Old Friend at Peach Blossom Spring. Inscribed upon a portrait of Yuanming:
Fame and profit are like discarded sandals—how could he stoop to bow for them in the dusty world? At his three paths, chrysanthemums are yellow and pines are verdant; much [is there to enjoy].
With few worldly concerns and a mind at ease, a single ladle of turbid wine makes me forget both heaven and earth. Who can recognize such a flavor?
I am resolved to remain intoxicated for a hundred years; there is nothing remaining beyond this body.
*Shaonianyou* (Youthful Wanderer). Following the original rhyme. Sent off Administrative Assistant Sa.

The pines grow cold in the misty forest, wild geese cross the autumn sky; in the halls of the Bird-Office, the guest finds it hard to remain. The mountains by the Huai River are green; at the sea gate, the waves are white.

The orchid-boat drifts away on the vast expanse; Yan-nan is not as near as Jiang-dong. Though the verses you sent have not yet arrived, my soul reaches the watchtower by the post station amidst the pines’ breeze upon my single mat and the moon through the vines at my half-window.

A Gift to the Daoist Master Chen Hanweng, whose divine eye possesses the power of spiritual discernment: We met by a boat at the river crossing; Zhang Changfang’s art of shrinking the earth was in vain, And Zou Yan’s discourse on the heavens was but empty talk.

The constellations and celestial paths were divided among his palms; a massive volume rested upon his ox-like waist. Yet he spoke of an aged Chan monk whose ears were far-reaching and who had lived even longer.

Master Renshan was appointed to oversee the two prefectures of Chang and Run; there, a host of eminent men from beyond the secular world took up the task of editing and supplementing the work in ten volumes.
Furthermore, you have not made any distinction between city and mountain retreats in your gracious dispatch of this instruction.

Not only do I recognize that your public service is fully equipped with both civil and martial talent, but I have also gained significant benefit from your guidance. Yet, how could it be right to leave you empty-handed?
I shall, despite my exhaustion, labor to compose these words at the end of this scroll to express my sense of reverence and submission.
North of Gu, the prefectures of Biling stretch into the distance; those who have held the tally and filled these posts have been men of heroic caliber.

Before the honored wine, they swiftly mastered the Three Histories; within the command tent, their excellent strategies surpassed the Six Tactics. It is fitting that the vessels of Mount Hua should now serve as farming tools;
the altar of the *Sao* poetry may likewise be raised even higher. All of Wu together celebrates the end of peril; the South Frontier has found its phoenix-like talent to serve as its wings.
Petition for the Construction of a Temple (with Preface).
This temple was originally established by the ancestral master Lord Pei during the Danning era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.

By the end of the Dabao era of the Liang dynasty, as well as during the Huichang era of the Tang, and again at the beginning of the Jianyan era of the Song, it had already suffered three instances of destruction by fire. As for the present conflagration...
The multitude of buildings no longer exist, and the two stupas have likewise been destroyed. Could this not be the fulfillment of Guo Pu’s prophecy regarding the four kalpas?

I humbly observe that while the Long River flows eastward, the mountains remain as steadfast as the Zhizhu Pillar in midstream; yet when the Great Teaching came from the West, the temple was transformed into kalpa-ash and returned to the earth below.
The Buddha cannot escape his fixed karma, and how can a person avoid the words of a prophecy? It is only by securing the necessary resources...
The foundations are complete and the provisions for sustenance are fully provided. Behold how the craftsmen’s efforts have converged and their labors have been accomplished:

the eaves and brackets reach toward the stars, and a brand-new Buddhist monastery encircles the peak of Mount Ao. The wheel-marks of the sun disturb the turtles and fish; the twin pagodas cast their radiance upon the horns of the dragon.
Thus, one may once again pursue the wind and moon of Nanxu, further strengthening the mountains and rivers of the Northern Gate. This is respectfully submitted.
At Huazang Temple in Changzhou, the Great Empress Dowager has commissioned the construction of the Longevity Star Hall, the Scripture Pavilion, and the Bell Tower.

Through this fundraising appeal, the ocean of lands within the Huazang [Avataṃsaka] universe—with its infinitely nested realms—is fully revealed; the vast winds and mists of Lake Tai are brought under her command, and the Hall of Longevity is fittingly opened.
To achieve this, one hundred thousand strings of cash are required to gird the waist; let us await the sight of hundreds of thousands of rooms providing shade from the sun.

Jade verses interspersed with golden inscriptions surpass the secret canons of the Shiqu Library; a jade tower reaches the Silver River, where one listens to the lofty resonance of chimes struck amidst the frosty moon.
May the perfection of giving gather auspiciousness, and may the imperial count extend through the halls of the vermilion palace.
A Memorial for the Construction of the Temple at Wuzhou under the Imperial Preceptor’s Hall:
The mountain commands the five prefectures, embracing vast expanses of wind and moon. The temple has been relocated twice, and fifty springs and autumns have accumulated in its state of ruin.

The Imperial Preceptor took charge of affairs and strove for renewal; the Chancellor assisted with the conditions for restoration. In seeking [the means], he was not stingy with his ink and paper, exerting great effort.
He passed away in the Lotus Palace. How brilliant! How excellent! We sing once more of his longevity, his years as enduring as the *chun* tree, forever nourishing his life at the *feng* steps.
The Elder Yong resided at He-lin. For many years, the various monasteries and meditation halls had been like ruined chessboards;
lamentably, no one had stepped forward to take up the task. The fundamental principles of the school were still as precarious as stacked eggs, awaiting someone with the resolve to restore them.

Once the debate was concluded and all returned together, [the Master] advanced to offer his mother the position, firmly declining it himself. Such a person, by means of the Dharma, secured the North Mountain and the North Fort.

Since both the host and the guest are fully present, the structure is especially magnificent and grand; it is fitting, therefore, to offer a virtuous eulogy to support its great beams.
Casting the beam toward the East: The red wheel of the sun drives across the sea to turn the Wondrous Peak. The vast earth and its masses of darkness are all illuminated through;
the myriad phenomena of the forested world cannot escape their tracks.

Casting the beam toward the West: Mount Lu divides its azure hues as they reach the water’s edge. What need is there to plant lotuses to continue the legacy of fragrance? The light of the river shines...
Huláng’s Flower Pond.
Throwing the beam toward the south: Here is the gate through which eminent friends first enter. How has the Way changed from antiquity to the present?
De-yún now dwells upon Mount Sumeru.

Thrusting the beam toward the North, one reverently bows to the Imperial Court and gazes upon the Sun’s Horn. As the scriptures are proclaimed from the lips of the multitude before a single incense burner, may we forever offer blessings to the Imperial Yuan and assist the Imperial Awakening.

Thrusting the beam upward, the sun, moon, and stars hang down auspicious signs. With all-encompassing protection, there shall be no peril of earthquakes or oppression; let us all join in prayer for long-lasting peace.

Beholding the mark of the white jade hair, I cast this verse for the lower beam: The various classes of beings, once without refuge, now have support. Having received the power of grace and looking up to your protection, Why should we not each advance in cultivation to flourish the Dharma-transformation?

I humbly pray that after this beam-lifting ceremony, the halls and buildings shall become ever more solid, and the scenery of wind and moon ever more magnificent. May both the mountain gate and the donor’s gate flourish together, widely welcoming streams of Chan practitioners from the five lakes and four seas.
May the destiny of the Buddha and the destiny of the nation prosper in tandem, perpetually extending for ten thousand years and a thousand autumns.
